$comment: single source of truth for the desktop release pipeline. the reusable ci workflows and scripts/*.sh all read this file, so adding a platform, a channel, or pointing at a new repo/org is a config edit here — not a workflow rewrite. see docs/RELEASE_GUIDE.md.
$comment_models: Only the BASELINE model ships inside the installer, so a fresh install works offline immediately without a download. Heavier models are optional: the app detects what the machine can run, checks whether an equivalent is already present (ThinkStack, Ollama or LM Studio), and only then asks permission to fetch one. Adding a model here puts it back in the installer - keep in step with domain/model_manager/catalog.py, and mind GitHub's 2 GiB asset limit.
$comment_rolling: Rolling tags are suffixed '-latest' so they cannot collide with the BRANCHES named beta and nightly. Git resolves refs/tags/ before refs/heads/, so when a tag and a branch shared a name, a bare `beta` meant the release: `git checkout beta` detached onto it and `git pull` reported a divergence that did not exist. Never name a rolling tag after a branch.
